location: Boundaries > Always (ps-e2e-run.py bullet) vs Design Notes > Record (version-level child fields list) vs cell-contract.md > Producers
issue: The spec gives three different answers for where `browser_mode` and `scenario_set` live. The Always bullet lists `browser_mode`=`sequential` and `scenario_set`=`full` in the same breath as version-level fields (`boot`, `boot_id`, `run_id`, `image_tag`, per-version `scenario_notes`). The contract's Producers puts `browser_mode` at version level and leaves `scenario_set` to `cells` ("the remaining per-cell fields"). The Design Notes list of version-level fields that ps-run-layer copies into every record (`run_id`, `boot`, `boot_id`, `boot_phases`, `boot_wall_clock`, `image_tag`, `errors`, `install`, `scenario_notes`) leaves out both.
implementation_impact: An implementer who follows the Always bullet emits `scenario_set` per version. The merge, which copies only the listed version-level fields, then drops it, so every pass/fail record stores `scenario_set: null`. The incomplete-record rule turns that into `inconclusive`/`incomplete-record`, no record is ever gate-grade, and `ready` can never be true. The unit tests won't catch this, because the ps-run-layer tests use hand-written child payloads. `browser_mode` silently becomes null in every record.
suggestion: State the placement in one place. `browser_mode` goes in the per-version child object and joins the Design Notes copy list. `scenario_set` and `scenarios_run` go inside `cells.<engine>`. Reword the Always bullet so it splits the version-level fields from the per-cell fields.

location: Boundaries > Always (ps-e2e-run.py exit codes: '0 only when every driven cell passes or E2E is skipped, 3 any fail, else 1')
issue: "Every driven cell passes" is vacuously true when no cell was driven. That covers a boot failure, a missing image without `--allow-image-pull`, compose missing, every engine dropped by the probe, or all engines in a version dropped. Today these paths leave `r['pass']` False and exit 1. Read literally, the new rule returns 0 for them.
implementation_impact: A literal `all(c.state == 'pass' for c in driven)` exits 0 on a version that tested nothing. Direct-run users (the quickstart TDD loop, Lapis 4 probe) see success after a failed boot. Any test that reads the child's exit code as a verdict regresses. ps-run-layer is not affected because it recomputes from records, so ps-run-layer tests will not catch it.
suggestion: Define exit 0 as: at least one emitted cell AND every emitted cell has `state: pass` (or E2E skipped). Add a ps-e2e-run test where the boot fails (stubbed `_bring_up_*` error) and expect exit 1.

location: Design Notes > Interim orchestration (Fase 2 wrap-up: 'today's --merge-only for Layers 2 and 5, --merge-only --layer e2e (report view) and ps-aggregate.py ...')
issue: The wrap-up is spelled out step by step but leaves out two steps. One is the cross-version Layer 1 static scan that writes `<module>-static.json`; contract Plan > Phase 2 wrap-up lists it explicitly, and today's run-phases.md runs Layer 1 once cross-version in Fase 2. The other is merging Layer 3 into `<module>-adversarial.json` before the aggregate. In Fase 1, Layer 1 runs per version only (`per_version[V].rerun` holds `static`).
implementation_impact: The docs writer copies this enumeration into run-phases.md and SKILL.md. The aggregate then reads a missing `<module>-static.json` (exit 2 '--static wajib') or a stale one from an earlier run, which yields a verdict on outdated Layer 1 evidence. Now that the `unscanned` gate is removed, a static file that is stale or narrowed no longer fails loudly.
suggestion: Make the wrap-up list follow the contract: merge Layer 3, then the cross-version static scan (`ps-static-scan.py --versions <configured>` to `<module>-static.json`), then the Layer 2/5 `--merge-only`, then the e2e report view, then the aggregate.

location: Design Notes > Interim orchestration (Fase 2: 'Then Layer 3 as today, spawned again after every loop-back unless the plan reuses it')
issue: Every plan call the interim defines uses `--per-version`. In per-version mode `per_version[V].layers.adversarial` is always `reuse: false`, because no per-version adversarial file ever exists, as the spec itself notes for `all_reuse`. "Unless the plan reuses it" can therefore never be true. Only a canonical-mode plan judges `<module>-adversarial.json`, and the spec never calls one; it would also now need `--session`.
implementation_impact: Either the four lens subagents are re-spawned on every Fase 2 entry, even when a fresh canonical adversarial file exists (a resumed session), or the LLM orchestrator invents its own freshness judgment of the adversarial file. That is the kind of manual judgment the skill forbids.
suggestion: Name the decision source. One option: one canonical plan call (`--session <t> --config <cfg>`, no `--per-version`) at Fase 2 entry, using `layers.adversarial.reuse`. The other: state plainly that Layer 3 is always spawned on Fase 2 entry and after every loop-back.

location: Design Notes > Interim orchestration (Fase 1: '--cells V:<scoped browsers joined by +>' vs Fase 2: 'group the scoped e2e entries')
issue: "Scoped browsers" is never defined. Only "run scope" and "scoped e2e entries" (rerun_matrix entries inside the scope) are. Fase 2 explicitly drives only the scoped entries, meaning cells that lack passing evidence. Fase 1 can be read as every in-scope browser of V, including cells that already have passing gate-grade evidence.
implementation_impact: The docs author will pick one reading. Under the 'all scoped browsers' reading, a passing chromium cell is re-driven every time firefox needs a rerun, which wastes a browser pass. Fase 1 and Fase 2 also then drive different cell sets for the same plan state. Under the other reading, the docs disagree with the literal command template.
suggestion: Replace `<scoped browsers>` with 'the browsers of V's scoped e2e entries (rerun_matrix entries with version V inside the run scope), joined by + in psm_e2e_browsers order'. This is the same rule Fase 2 uses.

location: Design Notes > Interim orchestration (Fase 1 end condition 'no scoped cell of V has a fail record of session <t> on the current fingerprint'; interactive infra retry 'appended no fail but a record with an infra cause')
issue: Both rules depend on per-record `state`, `reason` and `session` of what a run appended. No script surfaces them to the orchestrator. The output line lists only `appended` cell names. The exit code says only 'some fail' (3) or 'some inconclusive' (1). The plan does not filter by session. To apply the rules, the LLM orchestrator must open and parse the `.jsonl` histories itself, or remember exit codes across a session that can last a day.
implementation_impact: The orchestrator ends up hand-parsing JSONL, including corrupt-line and incomplete-record handling, to decide whether a loop ends. SKILL.md forbids exactly that ('jangan nilai ulang'), and the outcome is non-deterministic. Infra-cause classification (inconclusive reason, inconclusive-steps, browser-notes) gets re-implemented in prose.
suggestion: Phrase both rules in terms of the plan output, which already holds this information right after a run. 'A scoped cell of V has e2e rerun_matrix reason `fail`' replaces the session-filtered fail check. 'Reason ∈ {inconclusive, inconclusive-steps, browser-notes}' replaces the infra-cause check. Keep session out of the orchestrator's reasoning in this slice.

location: Design Notes > Interim orchestration ('E2E loop ended' and 'V's E2E step is due') vs Runner interim (Stop → exit 143, no output line)
issue: The interim orchestration does not say what happens after an E2E run that ends with exit 143. The usual cause is Budi stopping a hung job via `--stop-job` after the silent-log rule. The run printed no output line, so 'no E2E run of V this session printed the plan's current source_fingerprint' still holds and V's E2E step is still due. 'E2E loop ended' lists `skipped` and exit 2, but not a stop.
implementation_impact: Following the spec, the orchestrator immediately re-launches the same E2E run Budi just stopped, and it may hang again. In headless mode (silent-log rule stops the job), the loop can re-spawn indefinitely instead of returning.
suggestion: Add exit 143 to the interim rules. Interactive: a stopped E2E run ends the E2E loop for the session, unless Budi explicitly asks for a re-run, in which case it counts like an infra retry. Headless: a stopped E2E run ends the E2E loop, and the call returns as headless.md describes today.

location: Design Notes > Interim orchestration (Fase 1 loop end) / Boundaries (Always vs Never)
issue: The interim rewrites the Fase 1 end condition precisely: V's loop ends only when V is clean. The single operator exit it provides is for an E2E `fail` that Budi declines to patch. There is no exit for Layer 1, 2 or 5 blocking findings that Budi won't fix this session. The contract's 'Stop convergence' action, which covers exactly this, appears in neither Always nor Never, so its slice status is unknown.
implementation_impact: Suppose a module has a known Layer 2 warning-level or blocking issue that Budi defers. V is never clean, its E2E step is never due, Fase 2 and the wrap-up never run, and no aggregate or report is produced. Today's prose leaves that judgment to the operator, but the new precise end conditions remove it. A docs writer may also half-build Stop convergence, or omit it.
suggestion: Either add an interim 'Budi declines to fix V's Layer 1/2/5 findings → V's loop ends, report them as open' rule next to the E2E decline, or name Stop convergence explicitly in Always (interim form) or Never (deferred, with the interim decline rule as its stand-in).

issue: Nothing ties what `ps-e2e-run.py` actually emits to what ps-run-layer's merge and shape check expect. The ps-run-layer CLI tests replace `_spawn` with hand-written child payloads. The ps-e2e-run tests check `run_one_version` output on its own. The Verification commands are unit tests only, and the live tests are deferred. So the two halves of the new child↔runner contract (per-engine `cells`, version-level fields, timing keys, `image_tag` rename) are each tested against the implementer's own reading.
implementation_impact: A placement or naming mismatch passes every unit test and surfaces only at the first real run, as all-`crash` or all-`incomplete-record` records, which leaves `ready` false forever. Examples: the `scenario_set` issue above, `tag` vs `image_tag`, a version-level `browser_notes` list instead of a per-engine map.
suggestion: Add one contract test. Run `ps-e2e-run.run_one_version` (or `main` with `-o`) with Docker and `drive_engine` stubbed, as the existing tests already do. Feed its JSON output through ps-run-layer's real shape check and merge into a temp history. Assert that each record holds every Fields key, `scenario_set: full`, `browser_mode: sequential`, and a pass state that is gate-grade.

location: Design Notes > Aggregate / Tasks > tests ('rewrite e2e-file tests against histories')
issue: The spec defines `versions[ver].e2e_state` (`pass`|`fail`|`inconclusive`) and `reason`. It does not say what `versions[ver].layers.e2e.state`, `.reason` and `.errors` become. Today's `e2e_layer` emits `state` ∈ {`skipped`, `not_conclusive`, `pass`, `fail`}, and existing tests assert `skipped`/`not_conclusive` (test-ps-aggregate.py around lines 258, 269 and 285). It is also unspecified whether the console-error `advisory_note` survives, now that `console_errors` is per cell.
implementation_impact: Implementers will pick different vocabularies for the same field: keep `not_conclusive`, switch to `inconclusive`, or mirror `e2e_state`. The rewritten tests will encode whichever was picked, and consumers that read `layers.e2e.state` diverge from `e2e_state`. The console advisory may be dropped silently.
suggestion: Pin `versions[ver].layers.e2e.state` = `e2e_state` (values `pass`|`fail`|`inconclusive`, never `skipped`/`not_conclusive`), `layers.e2e.reason` = `versions[ver].reason`, and `errors` = the count of blocking findings from gate-grade `fail` records. Also state whether `advisory_note` is derived from the selected records' `console_errors`.

location: Design Notes > Timing (record wall_clock = finished_at − started_at; aggregate browsers[…].wall_clock reads wall_clock) + Child output in history mode (null timestamps filled with admission and write time)
issue: For a cell whose engine never started (boot or install failure, `browser-unavailable`, `crash`), `started_at`/`finished_at` are filled with ps-run-layer's admission and write times. Its `wall_clock` therefore spans the whole child lifetime, boot included. When such a record is selected (no gate-grade record exists), the aggregate reports it as `e2e_phase_durations[ver].browsers[<engine>].wall_clock`.
implementation_impact: CAP-6 exists to show whether boot or browser driving dominates. An engine that never drove would show a browser wall-clock equal to the full boot attempt, which is the opposite of the truth, and the before/after timing report could be misread.
suggestion: In the aggregate, skip the `browsers[<engine>]` entry, or set its `wall_clock` to null, when the selected record has no `browser:<engine>` phase. Alternatively, document that `browsers[…].wall_clock` is only meaningful when `phases` holds `browser:<engine>`.

location: Design Notes > Interim orchestration (Fase 1, Fase 2 and Quickstart command templates) / Code Map
issue: The command templates drop arguments that are required or that carry meaning. Plan calls appear as `plan --versions V --per-version --session <t> --config <cfg>`, with no module path and no `--reports-dir`. ps-run-layer calls appear as `--layer e2e --cells … --session <t> --config <cfg>`, with no `--module` and no `--reports-dir`, both required by argparse. The plan's `--reports-dir` has a cwd-relative default (`_bmad-output/psm-validate`), while ps-run-layer requires an explicit one. The Code Map's docs list also leaves out `references/adversarial-lens.md`, which the docs task edits.
implementation_impact: A docs writer who copies the templates either produces commands that fail (ps-run-layer) or produces plan calls that read histories from the default reports dir instead of `<psm_reports_dir>`. In the second case every cell reads `missing` and E2E is re-driven without end, one run per fingerprint, while `ready` stays false.
suggestion: Write every interim command in full (`<module-path> --reports-dir <psm_reports_dir>` on plan calls; `--module <module-path> --reports-dir <psm_reports_dir>` on ps-run-layer). Add a sentence that plan, ps-run-layer and aggregate must receive the same `--reports-dir`. Add adversarial-lens.md to the Code Map.
